Test fixture As a risk-reduction step, a benchtop test fixture was designed (Figure 5) to allow for evaluating the seal performance under a variety of representative tank operating conditions. The test fixture is built from two high- vacuum blind flanges. These off-the-shelf parts are designed for use in vacuum piping, and have a sharp lip just inside the bolt circle which bites into a copper gasket to seal when the flanges are bolted together. These flanges are modified by machining a groove in the top flange for the spring-energized seal and removing material to create a small chamber to hold a mating composite plate. The composite plate is 3.6 inches in diameter and of similar thickness to the inner tank wall; it rests on a brass spacer piece that may be shimmed to accommodate a range of plate thicknesses as well as investigate seal performance under small variations in working height. The seal acts directly against the composite to create an inner plenum. Two tubes allow for instrumentation of this plenum as well as the introduction of a variety of working fluids (air, liquid nitrogen, liquid hydrogen, etc.) at pressure to evaluate the seal under a range of conditions. The seal creates a separate annular plenum between it and the flange gasket, where a tube is connected to allow for pulling a vacuum. This mimics the configuration of the tank boss where inside the seal is pressurized liquid hydrogen and outside the seal is the inter-tank vacuum space. The fixture was fabricated in the RTRC machine shop. Figure 5: Seal test fixture Page 6 of 30 Approved for Public Release 1.4. Conformal tank conceptual studies: An XL-based tool was used to perform calculations for storage volume of conformal tanks. This tool was used to run various parametric studies with number of lobes and lobe diameters as variables. The outer dimensions of the tank can be estimated with this tool, and this was used to determine whether it fits in the storage envelope in a truck, behind the cab. It was determined that using a 3-lobed configuration, with a tank length of 2.6m, and a lobe diameter of 0.85m, it would yield a conformal tank of dimension 2.6m x 1.7m wide x 0.85 m, and has a capacity of equal to or exceeding 130 kg of LH2 with an assumed ullage. Other combinations of parameters (e.g. increasing the number of lobes) yield higher tank capacity, if needed. This tank size will fit into an envelope behind the cab of a semi-truck. 2.
